[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Substrate preparation  
- Use IBAD-MgO templates (CeO2/LaMnO3/IBAD-MgO/Y2O3/Al2O3/Hastelloy C-276) with biaxially textured MgO.

Step 2: Target preparation  
- Prepare PLD targets with nominal Y compositions x = 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2 in YxBCO + 3 vol.% BHO.

Step 3: Film deposition  
- Deposit ~300 nm thick YBCO+BHO films by PLD using a KrF excimer laser (λ = 248 nm).  
- Fixed deposition parameters: oxygen pressure 400 mTorr, target–substrate distance 50 mm, laser repetition rate 10 Hz, laser fluence 2.0 J cm⁻².  
- Vary Ts in 10 °C steps from 820 °C to 900 °C.

Step 4: Iterative optimization loop (data-driven)  
- After each deposition batch, measure Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) on patterned micro-bridges.  
- Update a Gaussian-process-regression (GPR) model with the new Jc data; compute Expected-Improvement acquisition map using BOXVIA software.  
- Select next Ts–Y-ratio conditions either at the acquisition maximum, in unexplored regions, or at empirically promising points.  
- Repeat until the acquisition map shows no further high-value regions (22 explored conditions total).

Step 5: Sample patterning  
- Pattern films into 50–100 µm wide, 1 mm long bridges using a 355 nm UV laser marker.

Step 6: Electrical characterization  
- Perform standard DC four-probe I–V measurements in PPMS at 20 K (and additionally 77 K, 65 K) under magnetic fields up to 9 T.  
- Define critical current Ic with 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion; calculate Jc = Ic/bridge cross-section.

Step 7: Microstructural analysis (on selected samples)  
- Prepare cross-sectional and plan-view TEM specimens.  
- Acquire STEM images to measure BHO nanorod diameter, number density, and tilt distribution.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Objective variable: Jc at 20 K, 9 T, B//c (A cm⁻²).  
- Input variables for GPR: normalized Y ratio and Ts.  
- Kernel: rational quadratic, k(xi,xj)= (1+d²/2αl)^-α; α and l fitted during regression.  
- Acquisition function: Expected Improvement (EI).  
- Optimization terminated when suggested points overlapped already-tested conditions and no high-uncertainty regions remained.  
- Optimum identified at Y = 0.9, Ts = 870 °C.

Title and Scope
- Objective: Establish a physics-aided, transfer-learning Gaussian Process framework (GPR-TL-PAM) to optimize and transfer the substrate-temperature (Tsub) window for epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7 (YBCO) films grown by pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) across four distinct chambers (R&D static and reel-to-reel), targeting Jc ≥ 3 MA cm⁻² at 77 K in self-field and predictable Jc(B) up to 3 T at 65 K with R² ≥ 0.81 after transfer learning.
- Materials: YBCO on IBAD-MgO/CeO2 buffered metallic substrates (biaxial texture Δϕ ≈ 1.7–3.6°; target Δϕ ≤ 2° for best performance) and single-crystal SrTiO3(001) with atomically flat surface.
- Key ideas: (i) Transfer learning to map equipment-specific Tsub scales into a common equivalent coordinate; (ii) Physics-aided modeling that operates on 1/Jc³ to unify magnetic field dependences across samples with similar natural linear defects and low-angle boundaries; (iii) Process strategies: oxygen stoichiometry tuning by post-annealing or oxygenation during cooling, texture/interface/stress management, and substrate selection.

Section 1. Experimental Design
Step 1: Define sample matrix and DoE across four PLD chambers
- Factors:
  - Substrate type: IBAD-MgO/CeO2 buffered metallic tapes (Δϕ bins: ≤2°, 2–3.6°), and SrTiO3(001) single crystals.
  - Growth parameters: Tsub (measured by chamber-specific pyrometry/thermocouple; nominal 780–900 °C), oxygen pressure pO2 (100–500 mTorr during deposition), laser fluence F (1.2–2.0 J cm⁻²), repetition rate f (5–10 Hz), target–substrate distance d (45–60 mm).
  - Film thickness: 220 ± 30 nm.
  - Cooling/oxygenation: (A) oxygenation during cooling (growth pO2 ramped to 0.2–1 atm by 500–550 °C at 5–10 °C min⁻¹); (B) post-anneal at 400 °C in flowing O2 (1 atm) for 30–60 min.
- Design of Experiments (DoE):
  - Each chamber: Latin-hypercube sampling of Tsub, pO2, F over 40 specimens per chamber (20 IBAD, 20 SrTiO3), totaling 160 training specimens; plus 40 additional specimens for blind test/validation (held-out, including at least 10 per chamber).
  - Include a focused sweep at higher Tsub (840–880 °C) on IBAD substrates with Δϕ ≤ 2° to test grain-boundary mitigation by higher Tsub while monitoring stress/cracking.
  - Replicates: At least 3 repeated depositions at the same nominal condition in each chamber to quantify process variance.

Step 2: Substrate preparation and selection
- IBAD-MgO/CeO2 metal tapes:
  - Select lots with Δϕ characterized by supplier or measured in-house by XRD φ-scans (YBCO {103}/{102} after growth). Two bins: high texture (Δϕ ≤ 2°) and moderate texture (2–3.6°).
  - CeO2-terminated templates preferred to ensure smooth nucleation; Ra ≤ 0.5–1.0 nm by AFM on representative coupons.
- SrTiO3(001) single crystals:
  - Prepare atomically flat TiO2-terminated surfaces via buffered HF etch and anneal (950–1000 °C, 1 h in oxygen), yielding unit-cell steps.
- Substrate dimensions:
  - Static: 5 × 5 mm² and 5 × 20 mm² coupons.
  - Reel-to-reel: 5–30 cm segments for short-length tests after establishing conditions; eventually 1–5 m for process-transfer validation.

Step 3: PLD deposition and inter-chamber calibration
- Laser: KrF excimer 248 nm; beam homogenized; spot size set to achieve 1.2–2.0 J cm⁻² on target; target rotation; pre-ablation 1000 pulses.
- Heater and temperature measurement:
  - Calibrate Tsub in each chamber using (i) contact K-type thermocouple pressed to dummy substrate (metal foil) at several setpoints, (ii) emissivity-corrected pyrometry cross-checked against the thermocouple, and (iii) in-situ reflection high-energy electron diffraction (if available) or ex-situ indicators (c-axis lattice parameter vs Tsub trends) as secondary checks.
  - Establish initial linear map per chamber: T_equiv = a_j + b_j T_meas (j = chamber index). Constrain b_j > 0 (monotonic). Parameters a_j, b_j will be refined by the GPR-TL model using performance feedback.
- Growth:
  - pO2: Start at 200–300 mTorr as a nominal mid-point; explore 100–500 mTorr.
  - Tsub grid: 780–900 °C; focus near the dome optimum identified iteratively by GP.
  - Repetition rate 5–10 Hz; deposition pulses adjusted for 220 ± 30 nm thickness (typ. 2000–4000 pulses; 7–15 minutes).
  - Target-substrate distance 50 ± 5 mm; vary deliberately in ±5 mm to capture chamber plume geometry effects.
  - Monitor plume with high-speed or long-exposure imaging to extract features (plume length, angular spread) for chamber descriptors.
- Cooling/oxygenation:
  - Path A: Oxygenation during cooling: increase pO2 to 200 Torr–1 atm by 500–550 °C; cool at 5–10 °C min⁻¹ to room temperature.
  - Path B: Quench in pO2 used for growth to 400–450 °C, hold in 1 atm O2 at 400 °C for 30–60 min, then cool.
  - Both paths executed on matched condition pairs to quantify oxygenation effects on Tc and Jc.

Step 4: Structural and microstructural characterization
- XRD θ–2θ: Confirm phase-pure, c-axis oriented YBCO (00l peaks); measure c-axis parameter (oxygenation/strain indicator).
- Rocking curve (ω): FWHM of YBCO(005/007) to assess out-of-plane texture; target ≤ 1° for STO; ≤ 2–3° for IBAD-derived films.
- φ-scans: YBCO{103}/{102} peaks to derive in-plane mosaic spread Δϕ and twin distribution; IBAD targets Δϕ ≤ 2° subgroup.
- AFM: 5 × 5 µm² scans for surface step/terrace morphology, rms roughness; identify interfacial smoothness differences.
- TEM (subset of 8–12 specimens spanning substrate, Tsub, and chamber): Plan-view and cross-section to quantify natural linear defect (dislocation) density and low-angle boundary spacing/angles (~2°); correlate with pinning signatures.

Step 5: Electrical and magnetic measurements
- Resistive Tc: PPMS or equivalent 4-probe, 1 mA; Tc,onset and Tc,zero; target Tc ≥ 89–91 K; ΔTc ≤ 1.5 K for well oxygenated films.
- Transport Jc(B, T):
  - Pattern 0.5–1.0 mm wide bridges (photolithography and ion milling or laser scribing for metallic tapes with protective mask).
  - Four-probe; voltage criterion 1 µV cm⁻¹; pulse mode for high J to minimize heating; validate with steady-state at lower currents.
  - Temperatures: 77 K (self-field and up to 1 T), 70 K, 65 K.
  - Fields: 0–9 T, B // c (field perpendicular to ab-plane) for all; optional B // ab subset for anisotropy check.
  - Extract n-values (E ∝ Jⁿ) as a quality indicator; target n ≥ 25 at 77 K, self-field.
- Uniformity (reel-to-reel tapes): Longitudinal Jc mapping at 77 K, self-field using scanning four-probe or magneto-optical/scan Hall methods on 0.5–1 m lengths once process is stabilized.

Step 6: Baselines and comparative protocols
- Baseline A (Single-chamber optimization): Independent per-chamber Gaussian Process Regression on raw Jc with inputs [Tsub_meas, pO2, F, d, substrate type], without transfer or physics-aided transform.
- Baseline B (Simple parametric physics fit): Fit Jc(B) to Kim-Anderson-like form Jc = J0/(1 + B/B0)^α for each specimen; predict at unmeasured fields via parameter interpolation versus Tsub.
- Baseline C (Linear Tsub mapping): Use a fixed linear inter-chamber Tsub mapping determined solely from thermocouple/pyrometry calibration, without learning from performance.
- Comparative: Proposed GPR-TL-PAM that jointly learns Tsub mapping, uses 1/Jc³ transform for field collapse, and includes non-numerical factors.

Step 7: Ablation studies
- Remove physics-aided transform: Train TL-GP on raw Jc; compare prediction error and calibration for Jc(B).
- Replace 1/Jc³ by alternatives: 1/Jc² and Kramer-type transformation to establish whether 1/Jc³ yields the best linearization/collapse; select exponent via cross-validation but report performance with exponent fixed at 3 for comparability.
- Remove chamber/substrate categorical features: Evaluate impact on transfer accuracy.
- Remove plume imaging features: Test sensitivity to qualitative chamber descriptors.
- Remove Δϕ information: Assess the effect of texture metrics on predicted Jc.

Step 8: Data analysis and evaluation criteria
- Primary targets:
  - Jc(77 K, 0 T) ≥ 3 MA cm⁻² on both STO and best IBAD (Δϕ ≤ 2°) subsets; report yield (fraction meeting target).
  - Predictive performance: R² ≥ 0.81 for Jc(B) up to 3 T at 65 K on held-out specimens from all chambers.
- Metrics:
  - For self-field optimization: RMSE and MAE of Jc predictions; maximum absolute error (MaxAE).
  - For Jc(B) curves: R², RMSE in log10 Jc space across 0–3 T; calibration metrics (predicted 90% PI coverage vs empirical).
  - For process transfer: Leave-one-chamber-out (LOCO) cross-validation—train on three chambers, test on the fourth; report ΔRMSE vs Baseline A/B/C.
- Statistical tests:
  - Paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-specimen errors to assess significant improvements over baselines.
  - Model selection by negative log marginal likelihood and Bayesian information criteria for kernel choices.
- Physics consistency checks:
  - Extract field exponent α from log Jc vs log B between 0.2–3 T; compare across substrates and Δϕ bins; expect α ~ 0.4–0.7 for natural line/low-angle boundary pinning regimes.
  - Correlate dislocation/GB metrics from TEM/XRD with α and J0.

Step 9: Process transfer validation
- Pilot-to-production transfer:
  - Stage 1: Train GPR-TL-PAM on 120–160 specimens (3 chambers), validate on held-out from those chambers.
  - Stage 2: Zero-shot prediction on 10–12 conditions in the fourth chamber (only thermometry mapping and chamber descriptors provided); then collect a small calibration set (N = 6–10) to update the TL mapping; assess improvement.
  - Stage 3: Deploy recommended Tsub_equiv for 1–5 m reel-to-reel run; perform continuous uniformity mapping; acceptance: >80% length with Jc ≥ 3 MA cm⁻² at 77 K, self-field; spot-check Jc(B) at 65 K, 0–3 T on 3–5 sections to confirm predictive fidelity.

Section 2. Implementation of Technologies/Methods
PLD growth and interface/texture/stress tuning
- Interface/texture:
  - CeO2-terminated IBAD templates or atomically flat STO to minimize interfacial disorder and enable uniform nucleation; verify via AFM terraces and reduced mosaic spread.
  - Growth at higher Tsub within stability window (e.g., 840–880 °C for IBAD) encourages surface diffusion, reducing low-angle boundary nucleation; monitor for Ba–Cu–O volatility or secondary phases by XRD.
- Oxygen stoichiometry:
  - Oxygenation during cooling vs post-anneal at 400 °C in flowing O2; select path that maximizes Tc and Jc while maintaining narrow ΔTc; use c-axis lattice parameter as a proxy for oxygen content.
- Stress management:
  - Control cooling rate (5–10 °C min⁻¹) and maintain compatible thermal expansion by buffer stack selection; limit film thickness to 200–250 nm to avoid cracking; inspect by optical microscopy/SEM for microcracks; reject cracked samples.

GPR-TL-PAM model architecture and training
- Inputs (X):
  - Numerical: Tsub_meas, pO2, fluence F, repetition rate f, target-substrate distance d, thickness, oxygenation path (binary), measured Tc, c-axis parameter, plume features (length, angular spread), Δϕ, ω-FWHM.
  - Categorical: Chamber ID, heater type (radiant/contact), gas-flow geometry (upstream/downstream), substrate type (IBAD/SrTiO3), IBAD Δϕ bin.
- Transfer-learning temperature mapping:
  - Learn chamber-specific affine maps T_equiv = a_j + b_j T_meas using a hierarchical prior that enforces b_j > 0 and shares information across chambers (Kennedy–O’Hagan style calibration within a multi-task GP).
  - Constrain the response to exhibit a unimodal “growth dome” vs T_equiv by using a GP with a squared-exponential kernel plus a quadratic mean function m(T_equiv) = c0 − c2 (T_equiv − T*)²; m parameters learned from data.
- GP kernel:
  - Product kernel over continuous variables: k_SE(T_equiv, pO2, F, d) × k_Matern(ν = 3/2)(plume features, Δϕ, ω-FWHM) multiplied by a coregionalization term for categorical variables (intrinsic coregionalization model) capturing inter-chamber correlations.
  - Noise model includes specimen-level heteroscedasticity estimated from replicate measurements and thickness variation.
- Physics-aided modeling for field dependence:
  - Transform response y = 1/Jc³ and train a second GP to learn y(B, T; X_proc) at a reference field grid. The 1/Jc³ transform is motivated as a monotonic mapping that accentuates low-Jc tails and linearizes power-law-like Jc(B) behavior expected from collective pinning by linear defects and low-angle boundaries; alternative transforms are evaluated in ablations.
  - For prediction at arbitrary B, the model outputs y(B) with uncertainty, then invert to Jc(B) = [y(B)]^{-1/3}, propagating uncertainty accordingly.
  - As a cross-check, fit parametric forms Jc = J0/(1 + B/B0)^α and Fp = JcB scalings (Dew-Hughes/Kramer) to the same data; compare residuals.
- Uncertainty quantification:
  - Use the GP posterior variance and propagate through inverse transform to yield 90% prediction intervals. Evaluate calibration via PI coverage versus nominal.
- Training protocol:
  - Standardize/normalize inputs; split data into training/validation/test with LOCO.
  - Optimize kernel hyperparameters by maximizing log marginal likelihood with gradient-based methods; implement priors for T_equiv map to remain monotonic and near thermometry calibration.
  - Early stopping based on validation NLL; Bayesian optimization for kernel selection if needed.

Non-numerical factors encoding
- Chamber design: coregionalization matrix learned for chamber IDs; plume imaging features included as continuous descriptors that capture chamber-specific plume geometry and gas dynamics.
- Substrate type and texture: categorical substrate type with separate latent embedding; Δϕ used explicitly as numerical predictor to account for grain-boundary pinning differences.

Implementation on reel-to-reel (R2R)
- Translate recommended T_equiv to chamber setpoints using learned a_j, b_j.
- For R2R runs, set heater zones to maintain T_equiv within ±5 °C along the heated length (verified by IR camera and embedded thermocouples on dummy tapes).
- Control line speed to achieve the same pulse exposure per unit length as in static depositions (equivalent total pulses corresponding to 220 ± 30 nm thickness).
- In-line plume view and downstream oxygen partial pressure monitoring to ensure the same plume–substrate interaction regime as used for model training.

Section 3. Feasibility Assessment
Resources and timeline
- Equipment: Four PLD systems (two R&D, two reel-to-reel), KrF excimer lasers, XRD with texture capability (ω–2θ, φ, rocking curves), AFM, TEM access (shared facility), PPMS and 9 T magnet for transport, plume imaging camera, lithography/laser scribing for bridges.
- Materials: IBAD-MgO/CeO2 tapes from established suppliers (Δϕ characterization provided), SrTiO3 substrates, YBCO targets (stoichiometric), high-purity oxygen.
- Personnel:
  - 1 PLD process engineer per chamber (0.5 FTE each over 6 months).
  - 1 characterization scientist (XRD/AFM/TEM scheduling).
  - 1 measurement scientist (transport/Tc).
  - 1 data scientist/ML engineer.
  - 1 project PI for integration and decision-making.
- Timeline (6–8 months):
  - Months 0–1: Chamber calibration, DoE finalization, substrate preparation.
  - Months 1–4: Film growth and baseline measurements; iterative model training after each batch; first LOCO tests.
  - Months 4–6: Ablations, physics-consistency analyses, TEM subset studies; R2R short-length trials.
  - Months 6–8: Pilot-to-production transfer validation on 1–5 m tapes; final reporting.

Potential challenges and mitigations
- Tsub accuracy and drift across chambers:
  - Mitigation: Dual-sensor calibration; frequent verification; include Tc and lattice parameter as soft sensors in the model to correct for drift.
- Cracking at high Tsub or thicker films:
  - Mitigation: Keep films at 200–250 nm; adjust cooling rate; monitor microcracks; avoid very high Tsub if secondary phases appear.
- Oxygenation variability:
  - Mitigation: Use both oxygenation strategies on matched conditions; monitor Tc and c-axis; choose path that yields highest Tc and narrow ΔTc for production.
- Measurement variability and heating:
  - Mitigation: Pulsed-current method with thermal checks; multiple bridges per specimen; replicate runs to estimate variance and feed heteroscedastic GP.
- Data sparsity in a chamber:
  - Mitigation: Coregionalization leverages data from other chambers; collect a minimal calibration set (N = 6–10) per new chamber to anchor T_equiv.
- Substrate supply/texture variability:
  - Mitigation: Bin by Δϕ; measure texture on each lot; include Δϕ as predictor.

Section 4. References to Previous Studies
- Foltyn, J. L., et al., "Materials science challenges for high-temperature superconducting wire," Nature Materials 6, 631–642 (2007).
- Hilgenkamp, H., and Mannhart, J., "Grain boundaries in high-Tc superconductors," Reviews of Modern Physics 74, 485–549 (2002).
- Dimos, D., Chaudhari, P., and Mannhart, J., "Superconducting transport properties of grain boundaries in YBa2Cu3O7−δ bicrystals," Physical Review Letters 61, 219–222 (1988).
- Goyal, A., et al., "Recent progress in the development of biaxially textured IBAD-MgO templates for YBCO coated conductors," Journal of Materials Research 16, 2746–2756 (2001).
- Iijima, Y., et al., "In-plane aligned YBa2Cu3O7−x thin films deposited on polycrystalline metallic substrates," Applied Physics Letters 60, 769–771 (1992).
- Dew-Hughes, D., "Pinning mechanisms in superconductors," Philosophical Magazine 30, 293–305 (1974).
- Blatter, G., et al., "Vortices in high-temperature superconductors," Reviews of Modern Physics 66, 1125–1388 (1994).
- Gurevich, A., and Pashitskii, E. A., "Current transport through low-angle grain boundaries in high-temperature superconductors," Physical Review B 57, 13878–13893 (1998).
- MacManus-Driscoll, J. L., et al., "Strongly enhanced current densities in superconducting coated conductors of YBa2Cu3O7−x + BaZrO3," Nature Materials 3, 439–443 (2004) — context for line/columnar pinning efficacy.
- Rasmussen, C. E., and Williams, C. K. I., "Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning," MIT Press (2006).
- Kennedy, M. C., and O’Hagan, A., "Bayesian calibration of computer models," Biometrika 88, 1–13 (2001).
- Bonilla, E. V., Chai, K. M. A., and Williams, C. K. I., "Multi-task Gaussian Process Prediction," NIPS 20, 153–160 (2008).
- Ward, L., et al., "A general-purpose machine learning framework for predicting properties of inorganic materials," npj Computational Materials 2, 16028 (2016).
- Kawasaki, M., et al., "Atomic control of the SrTiO3 crystal surface," Science 266, 1540–1542 (1994).
- Arendt, P. N., et al., "Rolling-assisted biaxially textured substrates for high-temperature superconductors," MRS Bulletin 29, 543–550 (2004).
- Ekin, J. W., "Experimental Techniques for Low-Temperature Measurements," Oxford University Press (2006) — transport measurement practices.
- Maiorov, B., et al., "Synergetic combination of different types of defect to maximize the critical current density of YBa2Cu3O7," Nature Materials 8, 398–404 (2009) — field scaling context (though with artificial pins).

Section 5. Criteria linking strategies to measurements
- Composition tuning: Tc improvements (ΔTc narrowing; c-axis contraction) indicate better oxygenation, typically correlating with wider Tsub process window and increased Jc; monitor via Tc and XRD.
- Grain boundary tuning: Lower Δϕ and higher Tsub (within stability) reduce weak-link density; evaluate by increased self-field Jc and suppressed low-field crossover (<0.05 T) where GB-limited behavior transitions to vortex pinning-dominated behavior.
- Interface tuning: CeO2 termination and flat STO reduce interfacial disorder; assess via reduced ω/Δϕ and higher effective cross-section (higher n-value and Jc).
- Texture tuning: IBAD-derived biaxial texture replicated into YBCO; verify by φ-scans and percolative Jc uniformity along tape.
- Stress tuning: Matching thermal expansion and controlled cooling suppress cracks; confirm integrity by microscopy; maintain high Jc in 200–250 nm films.

Expected Outcomes and Decision Rules
- Achieve and document Jc ≥ 3 MA cm⁻² at 77 K, self-field on STO and on IBAD Δϕ ≤ 2° using optimized oxygenation and T_equiv; if yield <60%, prioritize additional Tsub sampling guided by GPR posterior mean and variance.
- Demonstrate LOCO R² ≥ 0.81 for Jc(B) up to 3 T at 65 K using 1/Jc³ transform and TL; if not met, increase calibration set size in the held-out chamber by 6–10 specimens and re-train.
- Approve pilot-to-production transfer when: prediction intervals are calibrated (90% PI coverage within 85–95%), and R2R tapes meet uniformity acceptance.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Sample Preparation – YBCO films were deposited using pulsed laser deposition (PLD) with a KrF laser (wavelength 246 nm) under varying substrate temperatures (Tsub) and fixed oxygen pressure, laser frequency, and thickness within each series.

Step 2: Substrate and Chamber Variation – Five sample series were prepared using different PLD chambers (reel-to-reel or R&D type) and substrate types (IBAD A, IBAD B, or single-crystal SrTiO₃), with Tsub measured either by radiation thermometer (RT) or thermocouple (TC).

Step 3: Post-Annealing – All films were post-annealed: series 1–3 and 5 at 400 °C with oxygen gas flow; series 4 during cooling with oxygen introduction.

Step 4: Structural Characterization – Δϕ (full width at half maximum of YBCO(103) or (102) ϕ-scan in X-ray diffraction) was measured to assess in-plane texture; values are listed in Table 1.

Step 5: Electrical Transport Measurement – Four-probe method using Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) to obtain:
- Resistivity-temperature curves for critical temperature (Tc)
- Current-voltage curves for Jc at 65 K and 77 K, 0–9 T (B//c)

Step 6: Database Construction – Measured Jc, Tc, Tsub, Δϕ, thickness, and deposition conditions compiled into a database (Supplementary Tables S1–S2).

Step 7: GPR-TL-PAM Modeling – GPR models trained on source domain (series 1) and transferred to target domains (series 2–5) using location-scale (LS) shift coefficients; PAM functions (1/Jc³, 1/Jc², log Jc, linear Jc) tested to extend Jc predictions across magnetic fields.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Deposition method: PLD with KrF laser (246 nm)
- Oxygen pressure: 200 or 400 mTorr (fixed within each series)
- Laser frequency: 10 or 100 Hz (fixed within each series)
- Film thickness: 200–250 nm (measured or estimated, fixed within each series)
- Tsub ranges: 700–940 °C (varied within each series)
- Tsub measurement: RT (series 1, 2) or TC (series 3, 4, 5); authors note measured Tsub is not necessarily the true temperature and is treated relatively
- Post-anneal: 400 °C with O₂ flow (series 1–3, 5) or O₂ during cooling (series 4)
- Magnetic field orientation: B//c-axis for all Jc–B measurements
- Reference fields for TL: 0 T (77 K), 0.3 T (65 K), 1 T (65 K)

Experiment:
Step1: Objectives and Hypotheses
- Objectives:
  - Quantitatively map how coherent BaHfO3 (BHO) inclusions in PLD-grown EuBa2Cu3Oy (EuBCO) on IBAD-MgO metallic templates control vortex pinning and creep between 1.8–77 K and 0–14 T (extend to 31 T as available).
  - Resolve the trade-off between enhanced in-field critical current density Jc and accelerated vortex creep S as BHO evolves from ~4.5 nm nanoparticles (≈1.9 vol%) to splayed nanorods (≈4.8 vol%).
  - Identify a parameter window that maximizes in-field Jc while keeping S minimal for 20–65 K operation (target applications: high-field magnets, fault-current limiters).
- Hypotheses:
  - H1: Increasing BHO volume fraction from 0 to ≈3 vol% transitions pinning from weak to strong, raising Jc and the pinning force density Fp, with angular Jc peaks at the c-axis due to correlated nanorods.
  - H2: Beyond ≈3 vol%, rod splay and increased longitudinal correlation length enable double-kink excitations along/among nanorods, increasing creep rate S and lowering the glassy exponent μ compared with the optimal state.
  - H3: A Bose-glass-like state emerges around the optimum BHO fraction, characterized by a creep plateau and μ ≈ 0.7–1, consistent with correlated pinning theory, while undoped EuBCO exhibits intrinsically slow creep from dense dislocation networks and fine grains.

Step2: Experimental Design (Cohorts, Controls, Ablations, Evaluation)
- Film cohorts on identical IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy (Gd2Zr2O7/Y2O3/LaMnO3/CeO2/MgO):
  - C0 (baseline): EuBCO without BHO.
  - C1–C5 (composition series): EuBCO + BHO vol% = 1.0, 1.9, 2.8, 3.5, 4.8. Covers nanoparticle-to-nanorod evolution.
  - C6 (morphology control): 2.8 vol% BHO with modified growth rate to favor shorter rods (reduced length-to-diameter).
  - C7 (texture/GB control): 2.8 vol% BHO on IBAD templates with different in-plane mosaic spreads (Δφ ≈ 3°, 5°, 7°) to vary grain boundary (GB) density while keeping BHO fixed.
  - C8 (oxygenation/doping control): 2.8 vol% BHO with three O2 anneals (250, 300, 350 °C) to tune hole doping around p ≈ 0.15.
  - Optional comparative ablation (if resources permit): 2.8 vol% BHO + a light dose of point defects via low-dose He+ irradiation to test random-plus-correlated pinning synergy, without creating additional correlated pins.
- Sample numbers for statistics:
  - n ≥ 3 per condition for microstructure and magnetization; n ≥ 2 for transport Jc. Targets: ≥30 films total.
- Key observables and evaluation criteria:
  - Jc(B, T, θ): from both magnetization (Bean model with demagnetization correction) and transport (E = 1 μV/cm criterion).
  - Fp(B, T) = μ0 H Jc; Dew-Hughes scaling of Fp/Fp,max vs reduced field h.
  - Magnetic relaxation S = d ln M / d ln t (10 s–1 h window) and glassy exponent μ from collective-creep/Maley analysis.
  - Angular metrics: magnitude and width of c-axis Jc peak; lock-in angle; S(θ) signatures of double-kink.
  - Microstructure: BHO size/length/diameter, areal density and splay distribution; Eu2O3 precipitate size; GB density; dislocation density; twin boundaries.
- Decision rules:
  - Validation target: replicate or exceed reported benchmarks at similar BHO contents (e.g., Jc ≈ 31 MA/cm2 at 1.8 K, 5 T; ≈2 MA/cm2 at 60 K, 1 T) while constraining S ≤ 0.02 at 30 K, 1 T for the optimal condition.
  - Hypothesis support: observe monotonic increase of Fp,max and c-axis peak up to ~2.8 vol% BHO; at ≥3.5 vol% detect increased S, reduced μ, and broader splay distribution.
- Controls to ensure reliability:
  - Reproduce films across at least two PLD runs per condition to separate run-to-run variability from composition effects.
  - Use identical thickness (0.9 ± 0.1 μm) and substrate batch for all cohorts to control engineering current density and GB network.
  - Cross-validate Jc from magnetization and transport (agreement within ±15% after demagnetization correction).
  - Blind analysis on S and μ: two independent analysts apply the same pipeline to the raw relaxation data.

Step3: Film Growth and Composition Implementation (PLD and Oxygenation)
- Substrates and buffers:
  - 10 × 5 mm Hastelloy tapes with IBAD-MgO buffer stacks (Y2O3/LaMnO3/CeO2/Gd2Zr2O7/MgO), in-plane texture Δφ ≤ 5° preferred for C7 use.
- PLD system and parameters:
  - KrF excimer laser (248 nm), fluence 1.5–2.0 J/cm2 at target, repetition rate 5–10 Hz.
  - Substrate temperature 770–830 °C measured by two-color pyrometer (note: the “1055–1150” values provided correspond to Kelvin; calibrate to Celsius range above).
  - Oxygen partial pressure 200–300 mTorr during growth; target-substrate distance ≈ 5 cm; rotation for uniformity.
  - Thickness target 0.9 μm (±0.1 μm), monitored by calibrated deposition time and verified by cross-sectional SEM.
- BHO incorporation strategies:
  - Composite ceramic targets: EuBCO mixed with 0–5 vol% BaHfO3 (pre-reacted, phase-pure). Alternatively, dual-target, alternating bursts to tune average BHO fraction without changing EuBCO growth rate.
  - Growth-rate tuning for morphology control (C6): at fixed BHO vol%, increase repetition rate to 10 Hz and lower substrate temperature by 20–30 °C to limit rod length and promote quasi-nanoparticle morphology.
  - Splay control: maintain normal plume incidence; avoid substrate miscut to minimize extrinsic splay; accept intrinsic splay increase at high BHO fraction for C4–C5; quantify splay a posteriori by STEM.
- Post-anneal oxygenation:
  - Flowing O2 0.5–1 bar at 250, 300, or 350 °C for 30–60 min; cool in O2.
  - Verify hole doping p via Tc (onset) and thermopower at 290 K (optional) to target p ≈ 0.15 (optimal doping).
- Composition verification:
  - STEM-EDS quantification of Hf/Ba to estimate BHO vol%.
  - XRD θ–2θ scans for BHO-related reflections; Rietveld/Le Bail fits for phase fraction trends.
  - ICP-OES on ablated witness films (if available) to cross-check cation stoichiometry.

Step4: Microstructure Characterization and Quantification
- X-ray diffraction:
  - θ–2θ to verify c-axis orientation; rocking curves (Δω) and φ-scans (Δφ) to quantify out-of-plane and in-plane texture.
  - Reciprocal space maps (e.g., around (103)/(113)) to assess strain and lattice parameter changes from BHO mismatch.
- Electron microscopy:
  - Cross-sectional and plan-view TEM/HAADF-STEM at 200–300 kV.
  - Quantify BHO inclusion diameter, length, and number density; compute aspect ratio and areal density → matching field Bφ = n_rods Φ0.
  - Measure splay distribution: extract rod axis polar angle and azimuth; report mean and standard deviation.
  - Identify Eu2O3 precipitates (~20 nm), twins, and c-axis dislocations at GBs; quantify GB density via plan-view imaging.
  - Strain mapping: geometric phase analysis (GPA) or 4D-STEM nanobeam diffraction to map local strain around rods; correlate strain amplitude with Jc.
- Chemical mapping:
  - STEM-EDS maps to confirm BHO composition and Eu2O3 chemistry; line scans across rod/matrix interfaces to assess coherence.

Step5: Electrical and Magnetic Measurements
- Transport Jc:
  - Pattern 50–100 μm wide bridges by photolithography and Ar ion milling.
  - Four-probe I–V from 20–77 K in 0–14 T with rotational stage (θ = 0–90°; θ = 0° is H ∥ c).
  - Criterion E = 1 μV/cm; extract n-value from E ∝ I^n fits for stability assessment.
- Magnetization Jc and relaxation:
  - SQUID magnetometry (1.8–7 T) and/or PPMS VSM (2–14 T), 1.8–77 K.
  - Hysteresis loops with adequate field sweep to avoid flux-jump; use Bean critical-state model adapted for thin films with demagnetization corrections to compute Jc.
  - Magnetic relaxation: after field set and stabilization, record M(t) from t0 ≈ 10 s to 3600 s (≥30 logarithmically spaced points). Compute S = d ln M/d ln t.
  - Angle-resolved Jc(θ, B, T) and S(θ, B, T), focusing on θ near the c-axis to capture nanorod fingerprint and potential double-kink signatures.
- Resistive Hirr and Hc2 proxies:
  - ρ(T, B, θ) transitions to estimate irreversibility field Hirr(T, θ) for scaling; Hc2 proxy via high-resistance onset if needed only for Fp scaling normalization.

Step6: Data Analysis and Result Evaluation
- Jc consistency:
  - Compare magnetization-based Jc with transport Jc at identical (B, T, θ). Accept agreement within ±15% after geometry corrections; otherwise re-examine demagnetization and current transfer in transport bridge.
- Pinning force scaling:
  - Compute Fp = μ0 H Jc; plot reduced curve Fp/Fp,max vs h = H/Hk, using Hk = Hirr(T, θ). Fit to Dew-Hughes form Fp/Fp,max = A h^p (1 − h)^q to infer dominant pin types:
    - Expect correlated pin signatures (shifted peak at higher h) as BHO rods develop.
    - Track p, q across C0–C5; strong-pinning crossover should coincide with reduced power-law exponent α in Jc(B).
- Matching field and angular fingerprints:
  - From STEM rod density, compute Bφ; correlate c-axis Jc peak amplitude and location of Fp maxima with Bφ and temperature.
  - Analyze Jc(θ) peak width and lock-in angle; increased splay broadens peak and may increase S(θ ≈ 0°) via double-kink pathways.
- Creep and glassy exponent:
  - Determine S(T, B, θ) from relaxation data; map S vs T at fixed B (e.g., 1 T) and vs B at fixed T (e.g., 30 K, 60 K).
  - Apply Maley analysis: Ueff(J, T) ≈ kB T [d ln t/d ln M] with appropriate t0 to collapse data; fit U(J) ∝ Uc (Jc/J)^μ to extract μ. For correlated pins, expect μ ~ 0.7–1; for weak/point-pin dominated states, smaller μ.
  - Identify creep plateau regimes and compare across cohorts; test for increased S in C4–C5 relative to C3.
- Grain boundary effects:
  - Correlate plan-view GB density and dislocation networks with Jc and S in C7; verify that reduced GB density raises Jc but potentially reduces background pinning that counteracts double-kink creep.
- Statistical assessment:
  - Report mean ± standard deviation for each metric across replicates.
  - Use ANOVA or non-parametric equivalents to assess significance of differences between cohorts at fixed (B, T, θ).
- Success metrics for application-relevance:
  - At 60 K, 1 T, target Jc ≥ 2 MA/cm2 with S ≤ 0.02 for optimal BHO content.
  - At 20–30 K, 5–14 T, maximize Fp,max and maintain S below undoped EuBCO only if correlated glass regime is realized; otherwise quantify the trade-off.

Step7: Implementation Details and Critical Concepts
- Controlling BHO morphology:
  - Nanoparticle regime favored by lower BHO vol% (≤2 vol%), slightly lower substrate temperature and higher growth rate to suppress longitudinal coalescence.
  - Nanorod regime emerges at ≥2.5–3 vol% and moderate growth rate; maintain coherent interfaces by keeping lattice mismatch strain below the critical threshold (verified by GPA).
- Splay quantification and control:
  - Extract splay angle distributions from STEM; define mean polar angle and FWHM. Intrinsic splay is expected to increase with BHO loading; minimize extrinsic splay by normal plume incidence and polished, low-mosaic substrates.
- Avoiding parasitic phases:
  - Monitor Eu2O3 precipitates; if excessive, adjust oxygen partial pressure slightly upward during growth and refine post-anneal to maintain EuBCO phase stability while retaining target BHO fraction.
- Doping control:
  - Use Tc versus p correlation and, if possible, room-temperature thermopower to confirm near-optimal hole doping; re-anneal outliers.
- Double-kink diagnostics:
  - Look for enhanced S at θ ≈ 0° coincident with strong c-axis Jc peak; a reduced S upon small tilts away from c-axis suggests suppression of kink nucleation.
  - Compare S and μ between C3 and C5 at identical B, T, θ to isolate the effect of rod splay and density.

Step8: Feasibility, Timeline, and Resources
- Equipment:
  - PLD system with dual-target capability; KrF excimer laser; substrate heater to 850 °C; oxygen handling up to 1 bar; in-situ pyrometry.
  - TEM/STEM with HAADF and EDS; XRD with texture goniometer; SEM/FIB for cross-sections.
  - SQUID magnetometer (to 7 T), PPMS-VSM with rotator (to 14 T); transport station with rotator; access to high-field user facility (optional, 31 T).
- Personnel:
  - 1 PLD growth scientist; 1 TEM analyst; 1 magnetics/transport physicist; shared technician for sample prep; PI for analysis integration.
- Timeline (10–12 months):
  - Months 1–2: Template selection and calibration of PLD conditions with baseline EuBCO.
  - Months 3–6: Fabricate C0–C5; preliminary XRD/TEM; iterative tuning to hit target BHO fractions and textures.
  - Months 5–8: Full microstructure quantification; patterning for transport; initial magnetization and relaxation mapping.
  - Months 8–10: Complete angle-resolved measurements; fabricate and test C6–C8; optional irradiation comparative.
  - Months 10–12: High-field validation (if scheduled), data consolidation, scaling analyses.
- Risks and mitigations:
  - Risk: Over-splay or parasitic phases at high BHO. Mitigation: adjust growth temperature and rate; refine BHO fraction by target composition; verify coherence by TEM and strain mapping.
  - Risk: Oxygenation non-uniformity across the tape. Mitigation: post-anneal in flowing O2 with controlled ramp/cool; check Tc uniformity by multi-point resistivity.
  - Risk: Discrepancies between magnetization and transport Jc. Mitigation: improve bridge contacts, assess current transfer and heating; use pulsed current near high-Jc conditions.
  - Risk: Template variability. Mitigation: use a single batch of IBAD tapes and pre-screen Δφ; include C7 to explicitly account for texture effects.

Step9: How the Design Validates Conclusions
- Baseline vs composition series (C0–C5) establishes causality between BHO fraction/morphology and pinning/creep.
- Morphology control (C6) decouples “how much BHO” from “how BHO looks,” isolating shape/length effects on double-kink.
- Texture/GB control (C7) tests the role of background correlated disorder from GB dislocations, clarifying why undoped EuBCO creeps slowly.
- Doping control (C8) removes confounding from carrier concentration, ensuring observed differences are pinning-origin.
- Cross-method Jc validation (magnetization and transport), angle-resolved fingerprints, Fp scaling, and Maley/collective-creep fits provide mutually reinforcing evidence for the pinning regime and vortex-glass state.

Step11: Expected Outcomes and Decision Path
- Expectation: Jc and Fp improve from C0 to C3 with a strong c-axis Jc(θ) peak and rising Bφ; S remains low until the onset of significant nanorod splay and length in C4–C5, where S increases and μ decreases—signatures of double-kink activation.
- If creep penalty at high BHO is unacceptable, pivot to C6 morphology optimization to shorten rods and narrow splay at fixed BHO, or introduce a small fraction of additional random nanoscale pins (optional ablation) to frustrate kinks without sacrificing Jc.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Film growth  
- EuBCO layers (550–600 nm) deposited by PLD on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes.  
  – BHO-doped films: 1055 °C growth, 250 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.  
  – Undoped EuBCO: 1150 °C growth, 350 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.  
- (Y,Gd)BCO reference films grown by MOD on similar buffered tapes; BHO introduced via Hf-naphthenate precursor; 300 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.

Step 2: Microstructural characterisation  
- Cross-sectional TEM/HAADF and plan-view SEM/TEM to measure inclusion diameter (≈4.5 ± 1 nm in EuBCO; 12–14 nm in (Y,Gd)BCO), morphology (nanoparticles → nanorods with increasing BHO), separation d, grain size, twin-boundary spacing, dislocation density.  
- EDS mapping to confirm chemical identity of precipitates.

Step 3: Magnetisation measurements  
- All films cut into rectangular pieces (lateral size 3–4.5 mm) and mounted on Delrin disks.  
- Quantum Design MPMS3 SQUID magnetometer with field H ‖ c-axis.  
  – Tc determination: zero-field-cooled moment m(T) in 0.2–0.4 mT, sweep rate 0.5–4 K min⁻¹.  
  – Jc(B,T): hysteresis loops m(H) at fixed T (1.8, 20, 40, 60 K); Bean model for rectangular plates Jc = 20Δm /[w²lδ(1−w/3l)]; VSM mode used to reduce creep contribution.  
  – Magnetic relaxation (creep): after establishing critical state (ΔH = 2 T > 4H*), record m(t) every 4–10 s for 1 h at fixed (H₁,T₁); extract creep rate S = −d ln m / d ln t from linear fit to ln m vs ln t.

Step 4: Data analysis  
- Fit log Jc vs log B in the strong-pinning region to obtain exponent α.  
- Fit relaxation curves M(t) to interpolation formula M(t)=M₀[1+(μk_BT/U₀)ln(t/t₀)]^(−1/μ) with t₀ = 10⁻⁶ s to extract μ and U₀; construct μ(T,B) contour maps.  
- Compare experimental μ with theoretical values for single-vortex (1/7), small-bundle (3/2), large-bundle (7/9), half-loop (1), variable-range hopping (1/3) regimes.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Sample set: five EuBCO films (0, 1.9, 2.8, 3.8, 4.8 vol % BHO) and two (Y,Gd)BCO films (0 and 8.9 vol % BHO).  
- Film thickness: 550–600 nm (measured, Supplementary Table 1).  
- Applied magnetic field range: 0–9 T perpendicular to film plane.  
- Temperature range: 1.8–60 K for Jc(B); 1.8–60 K for creep.  
- Self-field regime identified via μ₀H_sf = μ₀γJ_sfδ/π with γ = 5.  
- Oxygen content y deduced from empirical relation 0.21y = 1.283+p (carrier concentration p from Hall data).  
- Doping consistency maintained within each growth method; absolute doping differs between PLD and MOD groups.

Experiment:
Heading: Objective and Hypotheses
Step1: Define goals and testable hypotheses
- Objective: Demonstrate that Cu-rich YBa2Cu3O7−δ (Cu-YBCO) thin films grown by PLD from a highly off-stoichiometric target (Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:4) form epitaxially embedded nanoscale cubic-phase domains dispersed uniformly in the orthorhombic YBCO matrix, acting as artificial pinning centers (APCs) that enhance vortex pinning at 77–80 K while preserving smooth surfaces suitable for sub-100 nm lithography.
- Hypotheses:
  H1: Cu-excess induces non-superconducting nanoscale cubic-phase domains (e.g., Cu-oxide or Ba–Cu–O-phase) coherently embedded in YBCO without creating granular high-angle grain boundaries; these domains increase the pinning force, raising JC(H) at 77–80 K and increasing the irreversibility field Birr.
  H2: Interface quality and strain control (LSAT at 780 °C, oxygen 100 mTorr; 40 nm film thickness) yield c-axis oriented films with four-fold in-plane symmetry (phi-scan), minimal mosaic (rocking curve FWHM ≤ 0.2°), and Δc < 0.001 nm, ensuring APCs are distributed uniformly through thickness.
  H3: Post-annealing (400 °C, 1 h, ~700 Torr O2) optimizes oxygen order in CuO chains (reducing δ), maximizes Tc, and suppresses granular secondary phases, achieving RMS surface roughness < 1 nm.

Heading: Materials, Substrates, and Equipment
Step2: Prepare materials, substrates, and instrumentation
- PLD target compositions:
  T0 (baseline): Stoichiometric YBa2Cu3O7−δ target (Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3).
  T1 (Cu-rich): Off-stoichiometric Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:4 (Cu/Y ≈ 4).
  T2 (comparative APC benchmark): YBCO with BaZrO3 (BZO) additions (3–7 mol% BZO), to benchmark pinning improvements against well-established APC systems.
- Substrates: LSAT (LaAlO3–Sr2AlTaO6, cubic perovskite, a ≈ 3.868 Å), SrTiO3 (STO, a ≈ 3.905 Å), and LaAlO3 (LAO, pseudocubic a ≈ 3.79–3.81 Å). Substrate size: 5×5×0.5 mm.
- Deposition system: KrF excimer laser (248 nm), fluence 1.0 J/cm² at the target; repetition rate 3–7 Hz; target–substrate distance 50 mm; heater capable up to 850 °C; oxygen process control 50–300 mTorr with fast valve; optional in-situ RHEED.
- Characterization: XRD (high-resolution, including rocking curves and phi-scans), reciprocal space mapping (RSM), XRR (thickness/roughness), AFM, HR-TEM/STEM with SAED, STEM-EDS/EELS for phase and composition mapping; SEM-EDS; RBS or ICP-OES for absolute cation stoichiometry; XPS for cation/oxygen states if available.
- Superconducting measurements: Quantum Design PPMS with AC/DC transport; four-probe microbridges; VSM magnetization loops; cryogenic probe station for angular Jc(θ).
- Device evaluation: Microwave microstrip resonators/filters on LSAT; VNA measurements of Q and surface resistance Rs at 77 K; e-beam lithography for sub-100 nm patterning tests.

Heading: Experimental Design (Baseline, Controls, Comparative and Ablations)
Step3: Establish baseline, comparative, and ablation cohorts
- Baseline cohort (B): Stoichiometric YBCO films grown on LSAT, STO, and LAO under standard conditions (248 nm, 1.0 J/cm², 100 mTorr O2, 780 °C, thickness 40 nm), post-annealed (400 °C, 1 h, 700 Torr O2).
- Cu-rich cohort (C): Cu-YBCO films from a 1:2:4 target under otherwise identical PLD and annealing conditions.
- APC benchmark cohort (A): YBCO+BZO films (3–7 mol% BZO) grown on LSAT to benchmark attainable pinning landscape from established nanocolumn APCs.
- Strain/thickness study (S): For B and C, thickness series: 20, 40, 80, 120 nm on LSAT; assess critical thickness and strain relaxation. Include STO and LAO at 40 nm to probe substrate effects.
- Oxygen pressure ablation (O): For B and C at 40 nm on LSAT, vary deposition pO2: 50, 100, 200, 300 mTorr; keep post-anneal constant.
- Post-anneal ablation (P): For C at 40 nm on LSAT, compare no-anneal vs 400 °C/1 h vs 450 °C/0.5 h; all at 700 Torr O2.
- Fluence ablation (F): For C at 40 nm on LSAT, vary laser fluence: 0.8, 1.0, 1.2 J/cm²; repetition rate fixed at 5 Hz.
- Grain boundary control (G): Verify absence of high-angle grain boundaries by XRD phi-scan symmetry and HR-TEM; include one intentionally granular film grown at suboptimal conditions (e.g., 680 °C, low pO2 20 mTorr) as negative control to calibrate diagnostics for granular defects.

Heading: Film Growth Procedures
Step4: PLD growth steps with parameters and process control
- Substrate preparation: Ultrasonic clean in acetone/isopropanol; DI water rinse; dry N2; thermal anneal at 950 °C in O2 for STO to reduce oxygen vacancies (optional). For LSAT and LAO, mild anneal at 800 °C in O2 for 1 h to clean surface; finish with UV-ozone for 10–15 min to remove organics.
- Target conditioning: Pre-ablate targets (T0, T1, T2) for 5 minutes at 1.0 J/cm², 5 Hz under 100 mTorr O2 to stabilize plume; monitor RHEED if available.
- Deposition window: Substrate temperature 780 °C; pO2 = 100 mTorr; laser fluence 1.0 J/cm²; repetition rate 5 Hz; target–substrate distance 50 mm; rotate target and substrate to homogenize deposition.
- Thickness control: Calibrate growth rate (nm/pulse) by XRR on test films; for 40 nm at 0.02 nm/pulse and 5 Hz, deposit ~2000 pulses (~6.7 min). Confirm thickness by XRR post-growth.
- In-situ cooling: Hold at deposition pO2 until below 450 °C; then ramp O2 pressure to ~700 Torr; dwell at 400 °C for 1 h for oxygenation; cool to room temperature at 5 °C/min.
- Safety and repeatability: Track substrate temp by pyrometer; use quartz O2 sensor; log all parameters. Grow minimum n = 5 samples per cohort for statistics.

Heading: Structural and Chemical Characterization
Step5: Verify orientation, texture, strain, phases, and domain morphology
- XRD out-of-plane scans: Confirm c-axis orientation by strong (00l) peaks; extract c-lattice parameter (target c ≈ 1.169 nm; Δc < 0.001 nm between B and C when interface/strain tuning is effective).
- Rocking curves: Measure FWHM of (005) or (007) reflection; target ≤ 0.2°; compare across cohorts for mosaicity.
- Phi-scans and pole figures: Assess in-plane four-fold symmetry; absence of multiple in-plane variants; quantify texture spread (FWHM ≤ 0.5°).
- RSM: Map around (103)/(113) to extract in-plane lattice constants and strain relaxation; correlate with thickness series.
- XRR: Determine thickness and RMS roughness; target RMS < 1 nm for Cu-YBCO on LSAT.
- AFM: Scan 5×5 μm and 1×1 μm areas; quantify RMS and peak-to-valley; require RMS < 1 nm and absence of particulates for device-grade films.
- HR-TEM/STEM cross-sections: Identify nanoscale cubic-phase domains in Cu-YBCO:
  - SAED: Acquire patterns from domains and matrix; look for cubic symmetry (e.g., Pn-3m for Cu2O or perovskite-derived cubic phases) and epitaxial orientation relationships with YBCO.
  - HAADF-STEM: Measure domain size (target 3–15 nm), shape, and spacing; estimate volume fraction and number density (domains per μm³). Uniform dispersion throughout thickness indicates coherent precipitation rather than granular inclusions.
  - STEM-EDS/EELS: Map cation/oxygen distribution; verify Cu enrichment in domains; probe Cu valence (Cu+ vs Cu2+) to distinguish potential Cu2O vs CuO; detect Ba and Y depletion in domains if present. Quantify film-wide Cu/Y ratio (goal ~3.6 in C cohort).
- SEM-EDS: Surface compositional uniformity and detect any micron-scale secondary phases; expect none in optimized Cu-YBCO.
- RBS or ICP-OES: Absolute cation stoichiometry cross-check on selected samples.

Heading: Superconducting and Vortex-Pinning Measurements
Step6: Transport, magnetization, and angular dependence at 77–80 K
- Microbridge fabrication: Define 10–20 μm wide, 100–500 μm long bridges by photolithography and Ar ion milling; confirm geometry by profilometry. Deposit Au contact pads for low-resistance contacts.
- Resistivity vs temperature: Measure R(T) from 300 K to 60 K; determine Tc (onset and zero-resistance) and transition width ΔT; target Tc ≥ 90–92 K; confirm no broadening due to granularity.
- Critical current density JC:
  - DC four-probe I–V at 77 K and 80 K; criterion 1 μV/cm; compute Jc = Icrit/(width × thickness).
  - Field-dependent Jc(H) up to 5 T; orientations H || c and H || ab; extract field scaling Jc ∝ H^−α; compare α among cohorts (lower α in Cu-YBCO indicates stronger pinning).
  - Angular Jc(θ) at 1–3 T and 77–80 K; identify correlated pinning signatures (c-axis peaks) vs ab-plane twin contributions; quantify anisotropy γJc = Jc(H || ab)/Jc(H || c).
- Magnetic irreversibility:
  - VSM magnetization loops M(H) at 77–80 K; determine Birr from the onset of reversible magnetization (e.g., when ΔM falls below instrument noise). Alternatively, use transport-based criterion at fixed voltage.
  - Kramer plots and Dew-Hughes analysis: Fit pinning force density Fp = μ0 Jc(H) H; classify pinning type (point vs correlated defects) and locate Fp,max and h* = H/Hirr at peak.
- Flux creep and pinning energy:
  - Magnetic relaxation M(t) under field; extract effective activation energy U(J,H) by log-slope analysis; compare U in B vs C.
- Target outcomes: JC(80 K, 0 T) in Cu-YBCO ≈ 3–4 MA/cm²; JC(80 K, 1.2 T) improved by ~1.6× over baseline; Birr(80 K) increased ~20% relative to baseline. Verify statistical significance.

Heading: Device-Level Validation (Microwave and Lithography)
Step7: Fabricate and test microwave devices; assess patternability
- Microwave microstrip resonators on LSAT:
  - Pattern half-wavelength resonators at 2–5 GHz; measure Q and effective surface resistance Rs at 77 K; compare Cu-YBCO vs baseline YBCO and BZO-APC benchmarks.
  - Evaluate nonlinearity (intermodulation distortion) at modest power; strong pinning landscapes typically reduce nonlinear losses.
- Lithography test:
  - E-beam define sub-100 nm nanowires and meanders; inspect by SEM; verify line edge roughness and uniformity; assess any pattern-induced degradation of JC at 77 K.

Heading: Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria
Step8: Statistical rigor, metrics, and validation
- Replicates: n ≥ 5 per condition; report mean ± standard deviation; use two-sided t-tests or ANOVA for multiple cohorts; significance threshold p < 0.05.
- Structural metrics: c-lattice parameter stability (Δc < 0.001 nm across C cohort), rocking curve FWHM ≤ 0.2°, phi-scan four-fold symmetry; AFM RMS < 1 nm; XRR roughness and thickness within 5% of target; absence of granular particles in TEM.
- Domain quantification: Average domain size (d), density (Nd), and volume fraction (f); uniformity across thickness quantified by coefficient of variation < 20%; orientation relationship indexed by SAED; domain identification by EELS (Cu valence).
- Superconducting metrics: Tc ≥ 90 K with ΔT ≤ 1 K; JC(80 K, 0 T) and JC(80 K, H) improvements vs baseline; Birr extracted consistently from magnetization and transport; Fp,max increase and shift consistent with nanoscale APCs; reduced creep rate S = d ln M/d ln t in Cu-YBCO.
- Cross-validation: Correlate domain metrics with pinning gains; verify that increased JC and Birr do not arise from granular boundaries (exclude by TEM/XRD/AFM); ensure oxygenation differences are controlled via O and P ablations.

Heading: Implementation Details and Key Concepts
Step9: Explain mechanisms and technical implementation
- Artificial pinning centers (APCs): Non-superconducting nanoscale domains embedded epitaxially interrupt vortex cores, increasing energy cost to move vortices and thus enhancing JC and Birr. In cuprates, strong, coherent inclusions (5–15 nm) with good lattice matching provide effective pinning without degrading connectivity.
- Cu-excess pathway: Using a 1:2:4 target enriches Cu in the growing film, enabling substitutional defects and precipitation of Cu-rich cubic-phase domains under oxygen-controlled PLD. The post-anneal drives oxygen restoration to the YBCO matrix, preserving Tc while retaining nanoscale Cu-rich domains as APCs.
- Interface/strain control: LSAT minimizes interfacial reactions and offers favorable match to YBCO pseudocubic lattice, yielding clean epitaxy. 40 nm thickness helps surpass critical thickness, promoting strain relaxation without forming extended defects.
- PLD specifics: 248 nm UV ablation produces congruent transfer under optimized fluence and oxygen pressure; substrate temperature and oxygen partial pressure control CuO-chain oxygenation and phase stability; in-situ RHEED (if available) monitors layer-by-layer vs 3D growth.
- Identifying cubic domains: SAED symmetry combined with EELS valence mapping differentiates candidate phases (e.g., Cu2O cubic vs CuO monoclinic vs Ba–Cu–O); the epitaxial orientation relative to YBCO confirms coherency and non-granular character.

Heading: Feasibility, Timeline, and Risk Mitigation
Step10: Assess resources, schedule, and potential challenges
- Resources and personnel: One PLD specialist; one microscopist for TEM/STEM; one superconducting measurement specialist; one device engineer. Instruments: PLD, XRD/XRR, AFM, TEM/STEM/EELS/EDS, SEM-EDS, PPMS/VSM, lithography/VNA.
- Throughput and timeline:
  Weeks 1–2: Target synthesis and calibration; baseline growths on LSAT/STO/LAO; XRR calibration of growth rate.
  Weeks 3–4: Cu-rich cohort growth; O, P, F ablations; thickness series initial.
  Weeks 5–7: Structural characterization (XRD/XRR/AFM); TEM/STEM on representative samples; RBS/ICP on select films.
  Weeks 8–9: Superconducting measurements (transport Jc, angular Jc(θ), VSM Birr); creep studies.
  Weeks 10–11: Microwave device fabrication and tests; lithography assessments.
  Week 12: Data integration, statistical analysis, and mechanistic correlation.
- Risks and mitigation:
  R1: Granular secondary phases (e.g., Y2BaCuO5, BaCuO2, CuO) forming at incorrect pO2/T. Mitigation: Tight control of PLD plume via fluence and oxygen; confirm composition by RBS/EDS; adjust post-anneal schedule; reduce substrate temperature slightly (760–780 °C window) if particulates arise.
  R2: Over-oxidation reducing Cu-rich domain stability. Mitigation: Optimize post-anneal temperature/time; compare 400 °C/1 h vs 450 °C/0.5 h; monitor domain persistence by TEM after anneal.
  R3: Surface roughening due to particulates from target. Mitigation: Frequent target resurfacing; pre-ablation; install plume shield; optimize laser spot size and scanning.
  R4: Ambiguity in domain phase identification. Mitigation: Combine SAED indexing with EELS valence fingerprints and XPS; consult known lattice parameters for candidate cubic phases; perform local lattice parameter mapping by nanobeam diffraction.

Heading: References to Previous Studies (pre-2025)
Step11: Cite relevant literature supporting design
- MacManus-Driscoll JL et al., "Strongly enhanced critical current density in superconducting YBa2Cu3O7−x films by BaZrO3 additions," Nature Materials 3, 439–443 (2004). Demonstrates epitaxial APCs (BZO nanoinclusions) and pinning enhancements in YBCO thin films.
- Kang S et al., "High-temperature superconducting wires with self-assembled nanostructures," Science 311, 1911–1914 (2006). Shows self-assembled BZO nanocolumns yielding large pinning improvements; benchmarking APC approaches.
- Miura M et al., "Mixed pinning landscapes in YBa2Cu3O7−x films with BaHfO3 nanoinclusions," Nature Materials 10, 706–710 (2011). Highlights nanoscale, coherent inclusions producing enhanced pinning and altered angular Jc(θ).
- Llordés A et al., "Nanoscale strain control of high-Tc superconductivity through self-assembled nanostructures," Nature Materials 10, 367–371 (2012). Connects strain fields around APCs with local suppression and improved pinning; supports strain/texture tuning strategy.
- Foltyn SR et al., "Materials science challenges for high-temperature superconducting coated conductor manufacturing," Superconductor Science and Technology 19, S23–S36 (2006). Reviews pinning strategies and thin-film growth considerations.
- Blatter G et al., "Vortices in high-temperature superconductors," Reviews of Modern Physics 66, 1125–1388 (1994). Foundational pinning theory; Dew-Hughes/Kramer analyses and angular dependence.
- Jorgensen JD et al., "Structural properties of oxygen-deficient YBa2Cu3O7−δ: orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition with oxygen removal," Physical Review B 41, 1863–1877 (1990). Oxygen ordering, phase symmetry, and structural metrics relevant to post-annealing and δ control.
- Veal BW et al., "CuO chain ordering and the superconducting properties of YBa2Cu3O7−x," Physical Review B 42, 6305–6316 (1990). Shows the role of oxygen ordering in the chains on Tc and transport properties; informs annealing protocols.
- Chrisey DB and Hubler GK (eds.), "Pulsed Laser Deposition of Thin Films," Wiley (1994). Techniques, plume dynamics, and process windows for YBCO PLD.
- Oates DE et al., "Microwave surface resistance of YBa2Cu3O7−x thin films," IEEE Transactions on Applied Superconductivity 11, 291–294 (2001). Device-level metrics and microwave performance assessment in YBCO films.
- Matthews JW and Blakeslee AE, "Defects in epitaxial films: The role of misfit dislocations," Journal of Crystal Growth 27, 118–125 (1974). Critical thickness and strain relaxation framework supporting thickness selection.
- Egerton RF, "Electron Energy-Loss Spectroscopy in the Electron Microscope," Springer (2011). Methods for EELS-based valence and phase identification in TEM.

Heading: Expected Impact and Validation Summary
Step12: Integrate findings and validation logic
- The multi-cohort design (baseline B, Cu-rich C, and APC benchmark A) with ablations (O, P, F, S) isolates individual contributions from composition, interface, texture, strain, and oxygenation. Structural data (XRD/TEM/AFM) validate non-granular epitaxy and domain formation; transport and magnetization quantify pinning gains; device tests confirm surface smoothness and microwave viability. Converging evidence across cohorts and methods provides a robust basis to conclude whether Cu-excess engineering creates effective, epitaxial APCs in YBCO thin films that elevate JC and Birr at 77–80 K without compromising lithographic compatibility.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Target synthesis  
- A ceramic PLD target with nominal cation ratio Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:4 was prepared by a conventional solid-state reaction (details of powder calcination/sintering not given).

Step 2: Substrate selection and cleaning  
- Three single-crystal substrates were chosen: SrTiO₃ (STO), LaAlO₃ (LAO), and [LaAlO₃]₀.₃[Sr₂TaAlO₆]₀.₇ (LSAT).  
- Surface preparation procedure not specified in the paper.

Step 3: Pulsed-laser deposition of Cu-rich YBCO films  
- A 248 nm KrF excimer laser PLD system was used.  
- Laser power density: 1 J cm⁻²; target–substrate distance: 5.5 cm.  
- Two growth temperatures were explored: 780 °C and 750 °C.  
- Oxygen partial pressure during ablation: 100 mTorr.  
- Typical film thickness investigated: 40 nm (strain study) and 120 nm (microscopy study).  
- Deposition rate: ≈1.6 nm min⁻¹ (not explicitly stated whether this value applies to both temperatures).  
- After deposition the chamber was filled with 700 Torr O₂; samples were cooled at 5 °C min⁻¹ with an intermediate 1 h anneal at 400 °C.

Step 4: Reference sample growth  
- A stoichiometric YBCO target (Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3) was used to deposit a reference film on LSAT under identical PLD parameters (780 °C, 100 mTorr O₂, etc.).

Step 5: Structural characterisation  
- X-ray diffraction (Bruker D8 Explorer) θ–2θ scans and φ-scans on (106)/(016) reflections to verify c-axis orientation and epitaxy.  
- Cross-sectional high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (Thermo Fisher Talos F200XG2) with fast-Fourier-transform analysis to image embedded cubic domains; energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy inside TEM to obtain local Y:Ba:Cu ratios.  
- Surface morphology and compositional surface spots checked by scanning electron microscopy (NOVA NANO SEM 450) coupled with EDS.

Step 6: Electrical transport measurements  
- Temperature-dependent resistivity R(T) recorded for 40 nm films; experimental details (current, contact geometry, criterion) not specified.

Step 7: Magnetisation measurements and J_C extraction  
- Quantum Design PPMS equipped with a vibrating-sample magnetometer (VSM) module.  
- Sample size for magnetic measurements: 5 mm × 2.5 mm.  
- Zero-field-cooled M(T) taken under 20 mT out-of-plane field.  
- M–H hysteresis loops recorded at several temperatures.  
- Critical current density calculated with the extended Bean model for a rectangular plate:  
  J_C = 20 ΔM / [w (1 – w/3l)] where l = 5 mm, w = 2.5 mm, ΔM is the magnetisation width.  
- Irreversibility field B_irr determined by linear extrapolation of Kramer plot J_C^½ B^¼ versus B at each temperature (data below 35 K excluded because of large uncertainty).

Step 8: Data analysis  
- Power-law fits of B_irr(T) ∝ (1 – T/T_C)^n and J_C(T) ∝ (1 – T/T_C)^s performed to compare Cu-YBCO and reference YBCO.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Cu-excess level: 33 % (Cu/Y = 4 vs 3).  
- Substrate choice for J_C/B_irr comparison: LSAT (microwave-device oriented).  
- Thickness for electrical/magnetic comparisons: 40 nm.  
- Thickness for TEM inspection: 120 nm.  
- All comparative superconducting property data shown in the paper refer to films grown at 780 °C; 750 °C data are only used to illustrate temperature sensitivity.
